methodology: Five distinct ayah first-pass comparisons against Qur'an 11:31-35 and Genesis 6-9 Hebrew/English (Sefaria). Absence is limited to checked texts, not all earlier traditions. No critical-edition collation or manuscript verification; no publication.

ayat.assessment: Noah denies possessing divine treasuries, knowing unseen things or being an angel, and refuses to judge socially disparaged believers. Genesis 6–9 has no equivalent self-defense; search early prophetic discourse traditions.
Opponents challenge Noah to bring threatened punishment; no exact exchange established in Genesis 6–9.
Noah replies that God alone brings punishment if God wills; Genesis 6:13 records divine announcement of destruction to Noah, not this public reply.
Noah's advice is unavailing if God wills misguidance; no source-specific counterpart established in inspected Genesis narrative.
Rhetorical interruption about alleged fabrication and individual culpability, addressed to Muhammad in common readings; do not misattribute this verse to Noah's speech.

staged_candidates.relationship: shared divine judgment setting with narrative contrast
staged_candidates.similarity: God determines destruction of Noah's wicked generation
staged_candidates.difference: Genesis gives God's announcement to Noah; Qur'an 11:33 is Noah's answer to challengers, emphasizing God's sole agency
